Unlike Gaussian methods that require complex depth-dependent covariance adjustments, Triangle Splatting uses a single smoothness parameter $\sigma$ for all triangles, ensuring consistent spatial influence regardless of depth or projected scale [S1].

The claim states that Triangle Splatting uses a single smoothness parameter σ for all triangles, ensuring 'consistent spatial influence regardless of depth or projected scale.' However, the evidence shows that the window function I(p) is defined based on the ratio of the signed distance field at pixel p to the signed distance field at the incenter (ϕ(p)/ϕ(s)). Since the incenter s and the boundary distances depend on the geometry of the projected 2D triangle T2D, the spatial influence (the shape and support of the splat) changes based on the projected scale and depth of the triangle. Furthermore, the evidence explicitly warns that if σ is too large, the support exceeds the triangle footprint and becomes 'globally supported,' which contradicts the idea of consistent, localized spatial influence. The parameter σ controls the falloff relative to the triangle's specific geometry, not a depth-independent constant influence.
